agent_role: Agent B - Task-Specific Validity vs Canonical Verifier Auditor

classification.summary: The task-specific adapter validates a closed construction proposal against one frozen relation, numeric-evidence bundle, construction provenance and budget. The canonical verifier validates a materially richer DelayedResponseRuleV1 plus graph, evidence, normal-reference, parameter and policy artifacts through twenty stages. Their shared concepts do not make their objects, decisions or authority equivalent.

task_specific.input_object: RuleProposalEnvelopeV1-like closed mapping plus ConfirmedRelationPrimitiveV1, ApprovedNumericEvidenceBundleV1, ProposalConstructionProvenanceV1, budget and allowed variables

canonical.input_object: DelayedResponseRuleV1 plus DelayedResponseArtifactCollectionProtocolV1, verifier policy and accepted library
canonical.output_object: RuleVerificationOutcomeV1 with VerifierResultV1 and optional accepted DelayedResponseRuleV1

runtime_authorization.input_object: accepted DelayedResponseRuleV1, accepted canonical verifier result, bound artifacts and verifier policy

validity_matrix.note: Different schemas are reparsed at each boundary; passing one schema does not satisfy another.
Task validity binds the confirmed relation; canonical validity binds graph nodes and typed roles; runtime binds the accepted verification subject.
Canonical Rule v1 has rule, graph-edge and evidence identities but no TASK-039E relation_identity field.
Task signs are explicit. Canonical MVP uses trigger state, graph direction and an increase-only expected-effect contract, so direct sign equivalence is not established.
Task validity requires one exact selected horizon; canonical validity binds fixed or interval lag to approved parameters and graph/evidence ranges.
Reference families and authority identities differ; equality cannot be inferred from the common concept.
Task proposal validity compares reference identities, while canonical stages inspect time, target, count and severity units.
Task validity fixes one runtime-logic family; canonical validity separately checks trigger, lag, window, persistence and output semantics.
Task validity binds the E1-derived bundle and construction provenance; canonical validity binds canonical evidence, normal reference and parameter artifacts.
Task proposal schema excludes free text; canonical stage 20 explicitly enforces the non-causal claim boundary.
Each layer uses distinct hashes over distinct subjects.
COMMON-42 is a later executable-equivalence portfolio, not an input to either construction validity implementation.
Runtime registry and receipt identity belong to the later authorization layer.
Both validity layers explicitly leave runtime unauthorized; only a separate authorization receipt can grant permission.
